anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De Oratione exists (only copyrighted Greer/O'Meara/Oulton-Chadwick); nothing to compare against. Sense checked against the Greek and cited Scripture wording.

apparatus: OT Father-texts (Deut 32; Isa 1:2; Mal 1:6) show naming without prayer-frankness.
Gal 4:1-5 heir-minor; Rom 8:15 Abba; Jn 1:12; 1 Jn 3:9 adoption chain.

choices.why: parrhesia = free-spoken frankness before God; the Savior 'announces' a new speech-status for prayer.
eikon-chain: saints image the Son-Image; keeps Origen's exact two-level imaging.
gnesios = legitimate, born-not-counterfeit; the Lk 'Father' dare requires legitimacy.

pass_a_gloss: No OT prayer addresses God as Father: the frankness is the Savior's announcement. Naming exists (Deut, Isaiah, Malachi) but sonship then is minor, blameworthy, under guardians until Christ's fullness brings adoption (Gal 4; Rom 8; Jn 1; 1 Jn 3). Luke's bare 'Father' warns the unworthy; 1 Cor 12:3 proves saying requires disposition (hypocrites, heterodox, demons utter; sinners cry Anathema by works). True sons say Our Father by works, heart believing, mouth confessing; formed by the Word they image the Image, carry heavenly image, shed the devil's seed for God's, and pray the whole life unceasingly as heaven-citizens and thrones.
